cases.sentence: Which report did the student say that the editor had revised?

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines Which with report, forming a nominal object headed by the interrogative determiner. Revised then merges with that object and projects its verbal label. Labels identify projecting heads rather than independently supplied phrase-structure templates; ordered children encode the intended linearization. Revised is entered as a whole-word participial verb, without decomposing its inflection. The object begins in the selected complement position, not in its eventual interrogative position.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded participial predicate and its interrogative object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent transitive little-v head merges with the participial predicate, and the editor merges as its external argument. This establishes the editor as the reviser and licenses the object's accusative Case. Had then merges above this domain. This analysis treats had as a finite perfect auxiliary occupying T and selecting the participial predicate; it does not posit an additional auxiliary-head movement or a separately realized perfect head. The embedded subject remains in its first-merged position at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the embedded external argument and finite perfect auxiliary.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Before the embedded verbal phase becomes inaccessible, its edge feature internally merges the interrogative object at the outer edge of little-v. The lower object occurrence is retained but unpronounced. Finite T agrees with the editor, values nominative Case, and internally merges that subject at its edge to satisfy its subject requirement. The subject's lower occurrence also remains silent. These operations draw on distinct positions already present in the preceding workspace. The verbal edge step is required here because subsequent extraction must cross both the embedded verbal phase and the embedded clause boundary.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the embedded subject and make the object accessible at the embedded phase edge.

values.interpretation: intermediate escape position without interrogative scope

derivationStages.stageRecord: The declarative complementizer that merges with the embedded T projection. Its edge feature internally merges the interrogative phrase from the already established verbal edge to the clause edge. This occurrence is an intermediate escape position, not the scope position of an embedded question: that remains declarative, and had remains below the embedded subject. Extraction is from the object position, so retaining overt that does not create the subject-extraction configuration associated with the that-trace restriction. The previous verbal-edge copy becomes unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Build the declarative complement clause and its wh escape edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Say selects the completed declarative C projection as its complement. A silent matrix little-v head merges with this predicate, and the student merges as the external argument of saying. Say is a bridge predicate in this construction: its finite clausal complement supports extraction through the complement's accessible edge. Which report is therefore the object of revised, not an additional nominal object of say. The matrix subject is still in its first-merged position.
derivationStages.statement: Merge the bridge predicate and its matrix external argument.

values.commitment: finite do in T; lexical verb remains bare and does not raise to T

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verbal edge feature first internally merges which report from the embedded clause edge to the outer edge of matrix little-v, preserving accessibility across the matrix verbal phase. Past T is then merged, with auxiliary do supplied in its whole-word finite form did. This is the do-support commitment of the analysis: lexical say stays in the verbal domain, and the question's tense-bearing auxiliary is independently available in T for inversion. T agrees with the student, licenses nominative Case, and internally merges the subject at its edge. The earlier wh occurrence and lower subject occurrence are retained silently. The matrix verbal-edge wh occurrence remains pronounced provisionally until the scope position is built.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the matrix verbal escape edge and finite subject position.

values.chainOrder: from highest scope occurrence through successive phase edges to the selected object
values.interpretation: interrogative report variable interpreted as the embedded object's argument

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent interrogative C merges with the matrix T projection. Its inversion requirement attracts the finite auxiliary from the previously established T position, forming a C-headed complex with did and leaving a silent lower auxiliary copy. Its interrogative edge requirement then internally merges which report from the matrix verbal edge into the matrix clause edge. The highest wh occurrence receives pronunciation and matrix interrogative scope; all earlier wh copies remain silent, with the lowest copy preserving the selected object position of revised. Both subjects are pronounced only in their finite T-edge positions. The completed structure asks for the report such that the student said that the editor had revised it. The past perfect remains inside the declarative complement, and no embedded subject–auxiliary inversion occurs. Reading the pronounced terminals yields exactly the supplied tokens.
derivationStages.statement: Complete matrix inversion and the long-distance interrogative dependency.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject is a DP headed by Una, with profesora projecting NP; the object is a DP headed by distributive cada, with informe projecting NP. Each DP contains a D′, and each noun projects N′. Revisó is initially the V head: its finite spelling is already present, while its syntactic association with I will be established by head movement. The object occupies the complement of V, and the subject is generated in Spec-VP under the VP-internal subject hypothesis. An initially unfilled subject position is available in IP. Silent I carries preterite indicative tense and third-person singular agreement features; silent declarative C selects IP. First, the verb's argument structure assigns the external Agent role to the subject and the internal Theme role to the object. Second, V governs its object and licenses structural accusative Case, although this Case has no separate overt exponent on cada informe. The indefinite subject introduces an existential interpretation, while cada supplies distributive universal quantification; their relative scope is not yet fixed.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the base-generated clause and its argument structure.

relations.relation: V-to-I movement chain and trace licensing

derivationStages.stageRecord: Revisó moves from its previously established V position and left-adjoins to I, creating a complex I head. Its original position becomes a silent head trace. The movement chain connects the pronounced verb in I with that trace; movement to the immediately higher inflectional head respects the Head Movement Constraint. The raised complex head properly governs the V trace. The finite lexical form revisó checks the preterite indicative and third-person singular features of I. This analysis does not split the input word into separately realized stem and suffix terminals: the abstract inflectional head remains silent.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the finite verb from V to I.

relations.relation: nominative Case, agreement, and subject requirement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject DP moves from Spec-VP to Spec-IP, leaving a silent DP trace in its external theta position. Its determiner and nominal restriction move together, preserving Una profesora as one constituent. The resulting A-chain connects the raised subject to its theta-marked trace and licenses that trace by antecedent government. Finite I then licenses nominative Case on the raised subject and agrees with its third-person singular features; the filled Spec-IP satisfies the subject requirement of the finite clause. The subject receives no additional theta role in Spec-IP. The resulting pronounced order is exactly Una profesora revisó cada informe. No reflexive or pronominal antecedent dependency requires an additional Binding Theory relation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the subject to Spec-IP and establish the overt sentence.

values.interpretation: upper quantifier binds lower argument variable

values.reading: There is a female teacher who reviewed every report.

derivationStages.stageRecord: At LF, cada informe undergoes Quantifier Raising from its established object position to a VP-adjoined position. The upper occurrence c-commands the object position but remains below the subject in Spec-IP. To retain both LF scope and the exact overt input in one workspace, the QR chain uses copy notation: its upper DP is silent at PF, while its lower lexical copy remains pronounced and is interpreted as the bound argument variable rather than as a second quantifier. This is a notational representation of the GB operator–variable dependency, not overt object fronting. First, the QR relation establishes the A′-chain and variable binding between the upper operator and lower object occurrence; the lower occurrence retains the object's theta and Case licensing. Second, the scope relation places the existential subject above the universal object. The reading is that there is a female teacher who reviewed every report; the same teacher satisfies the claim for all relevant reports. Scope variation does not require distinct lexical structures for Una or cada, and no additional referential coindexation is introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the subject-wide-scope reading by VP-level Quantifier Raising.
